questions.question: Explain the difference between quantitative and qualitative data, giving one strength and one limitation of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Quantitative: numerical, easy to analyse and compare, objective. But lacks depth and context. Qualitative: rich, detailed, captures experiences. But harder to analyse, subjective. Both types are valuable - mixed methods provide a more complete picture.

questions.question: Describe three ethical issues that psychologists must consider when conducting research.
questions.correctAnswer: Informed consent: participants must know what they are agreeing to - without it, their autonomy is violated. Deception: misleading participants undermines trust - only justified if the research question cannot be addressed otherwise. Protection from harm: researchers must minimise risks.

questions.question: A study finds mean = 15, median = 12, mode = 10. Explain what these results suggest about the distribution of the data.
questions.correctAnswer: Mean > median > mode suggests a positively skewed distribution - a few high scores are pulling the mean upwards. The median (12) is a better measure of central tendency here because it is less affected by the extreme high scores than the mean (15).

questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: explain key ethical principles (consent, deception, protection, withdrawal); argue they are necessary (Milgram's study caused extreme stress); argue they may be too strict (some important research could not be conducted, deception sometimes necessary for valid results); conclude: ethical guidelines are essential but should be proportionate - researchers should seek the least deceptive approach while still being able to investigate important questions.
